title: Hash table with separate chaining
source: Week 8 lecture (Hash): collisions, separate chaining, load factor 0.7

tests.name: Resizing
Overwrite an existing key
tests.hint: If the key is already in its cell, replace the value instead of adding a second pair.

tests.name: remove from the middle of a chain
tests.setup:
t = HashTable(10)
t.put(3, "a")
t.put(13, "b")
t.put(23, "c")
t.remove(13)

tests.name: Exactly 0.7 doesn't resize
Rehashing moves pairs to new cells
tests.hint: After resizing, every pair goes into the cell for the NEW size.

tests.name: Many resizes
String keys
50 000 puts and gets
tests.data:
import random
random.seed(808)
keys = random.sample(range(10**9), 50000)
look = keys[::3] + random.sample(range(10**9), 20000)
tests.expr: (len(t), len(t.buckets), sum(t.get(k) or 0 for k in look), t.get(-5))
tests.hint: Without resizing, every cell's chain grows to thousands of pairs and each lookup becomes O(N).
